quests.question: The pilot spotted ___ active volcano below.
quests.sentence: The pilot spotted ___ active volcano below.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Active' starts with the vowel 'a', so we write 'an active volcano'.

quests.question: We sailed across ___ Pacific Ocean.
quests.hint: Oceans always take 'the' - they are named bodies of water.
quests.explanation: All named oceans use 'the': the Pacific Ocean, the Atlantic Ocean, the Indian Ocean. The same rule applies to seas (the Red Sea, the Caribbean Sea).

quests.question: They climbed ___ Mount Everest last spring.
quests.sentence: They climbed ___ Mount Everest last spring.
quests.hint: Single, individually named mountains take no article.
quests.explanation: Individual mountains with 'Mount' or 'Mt.' in their name take no article: Mount Everest, Mount Fuji, Mount Kilimanjaro. But mountain ranges take 'the': the Alps, the Himalayas.

quests.question: They discovered ___ oasis in the desert.
quests.sentence: They discovered ___ oasis in the desert.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Oasis' starts with the vowel 'o', so we write 'an oasis'.

quests.question: The caravan crossed ___ Sahara Desert.
quests.explanation: Named deserts always use 'the': the Sahara Desert, the Gobi Desert, the Atacama Desert. They follow the same rule as oceans and mountain ranges.

quests.question: She was born in ___ France.
quests.hint: Standard country names take no article.
quests.explanation: Most country names take no article: France, Brazil, Japan, Australia, India. Exceptions include countries with 'the' built into their name (the USA, the UK, the Netherlands).

quests.question: He mapped ___ frozen landscape.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Frozen' starts with 'f', so we write 'a frozen landscape'.

quests.question: We reached ___ highest point on the trail.
quests.sentence: We reached ___ highest point on the trail.
quests.explanation: Superlative adjectives (the highest, the deepest, the longest, the best) always use 'the' because they identify something unique - the one that is most extreme.

quests.question: They spent the summer in ___ Asia.
quests.sentence: They spent the summer in ___ Asia.
quests.explanation: Continents take no article: Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Australia, Antarctica.

quests.question: They live in ___ humid climate.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. In 'humid', the 'h' is fully pronounced (unlike in 'honest' or 'hour'), so use 'a humid climate'.

quests.question: They trekked through ___ Alps.
quests.explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the': the Alps, the Himalayas, the Andes, the Rockies. Individual mountains do not: Mount Everest, Ben Nevis, Kilimanjaro.

quests.question: A probe was sent to study ___ Mars.
quests.sentence: A probe was sent to study ___ Mars.
quests.hint: Individual planet names take no article.
quests.explanation: Planets named after classical figures take no article: Mars, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune. Note: Earth sometimes uses 'the' (the Earth), but other planets do not.

quests.question: It was ___ alpine environment.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Alpine' starts with the vowel 'a', so we write 'an alpine environment'.

quests.question: He explored ___ Amazon River.
quests.explanation: All named rivers use 'the': the Amazon, the Nile, the Thames, the Mississippi, the Danube.

quests.question: They sailed to ___ Madagascar.
quests.hint: Single, individually named islands take no article.
quests.explanation: Single named islands take no article: Madagascar, Cuba, Iceland, Greenland, Bali. Island groups (plural) take 'the': the Bahamas, the Philippines, the Maldives.

quests.question: He spotted ___ rocky island ahead.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Rocky' starts with 'r', so we write 'a rocky island'.

quests.question: The ship crossed ___ equator.
quests.hint: The equator is a unique geographical line - there is only one.
quests.explanation: Unique geographical lines and zones take 'the': the equator, the North Pole, the South Pole, the Arctic Circle, the Tropic of Cancer.

quests.question: She studied ___ biology.
quests.explanation: Scientific and academic subjects take no article: biology, chemistry, mathematics, history, geography, economics.

quests.question: They found ___ inland route.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Inland' starts with the vowel 'i', so we write 'an inland route'.

quests.question: The satellite orbited ___ Earth.
quests.hint: In an astronomical context, Earth is referred to as 'the Earth'.
quests.explanation: When 'Earth' is used in an astronomical or scientific context - especially with a verb like 'orbit' - it takes 'the'. Compare: 'Earth is a planet' (no article, planet name) vs. 'orbiting the Earth' (the, referring to our specific world).

quests.question: ___ nature has a way of healing itself.
quests.sentence: ___ nature has a way of healing itself.
quests.hint: 'Nature' used as a general, abstract concept takes no article.
quests.explanation: When 'nature' refers to the natural world in a general, philosophical sense, no article is used: 'Nature is beautiful', 'Respect nature'. Compare: 'the nature of the problem' (the, with a modifier).

quests.question: She designed ___ green rooftop garden.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Green' starts with 'g', so we write 'a green rooftop garden'.

quests.question: A tanker navigated ___ Suez Canal.
quests.explanation: Named canals take 'the': the Suez Canal, the Panama Canal, the English Channel. They follow the same rule as rivers and oceans.

quests.question: Tourists often visit ___ Mount Fuji.
quests.hint: Individual mountains with 'Mount' in their name take no article.
quests.explanation: No article is used with 'Mount' + proper name: Mount Fuji, Mount Rushmore, Mount Olympus. Remember: mountain ranges take 'the' (the Alps), but individual peaks do not.

quests.question: It was ___ enormous challenge.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Enormous' starts with the vowel 'e', so we write 'an enormous challenge'.

quests.question: We visited ___ Bahamas last winter.
quests.hint: Groups of islands with a plural name take 'the'.
quests.explanation: Island groups and archipelagos with plural names take 'the': the Bahamas, the Maldives, the Philippines, the Canary Islands. Single islands do not: Cuba, Iceland, Bali.

quests.question: They camped beside ___ Lake Baikal.
quests.hint: Individual lakes named with 'Lake' + proper name take no article.
quests.explanation: Individual named lakes take no article when 'Lake' comes first: Lake Baikal, Lake Victoria, Lake Superior. Compare rivers, which always take 'the': the Thames, the Nile.

quests.question: This is ___ dry and dusty region.
quests.sentence: This is ___ dry and dusty region.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Dry' starts with 'd', so we write 'a dry and dusty region'.

quests.question: ___ North Pole is covered in ice.
quests.sentence: ___ North Pole is covered in ice.
quests.hint: The North Pole is a unique geographical point - there is only one.
quests.explanation: Unique geographical poles and extreme points take 'the': the North Pole, the South Pole. They are one-of-a-kind locations.

quests.question: She grew up in ___ London.
quests.explanation: Cities and towns never take an article: London, Paris, Tokyo, Cairo, Sydney. The same rule applies to villages, towns, and most named settlements.
